positive: A package-owned resolver returns a typed, fingerprinted receipt containing provider identity, official source/revision/commit, bundle fingerprint, trust posture, artifact-identity status, verified pack root, network_used false, and categorical issues.
Installed-package, managed-payload, and source-checkout providers resolve independently of the process current working directory and use deterministic documented precedence.
The source-checkout provider derives its root from module location plus repository sentinels and reports development-local unless stronger authenticated identity evidence is supplied.
The managed-payload provider resolves only the versioned shared install root and reports corruption-detection-only unless an exact qualifying ownership or installation receipt is verified.
Package outer integrity and bundle inner integrity are both checked before a provider can be selected, using exact expected/declared/actual inventory equality and safe regular-file paths.

Focused proof covers each provider, precedence, current-working-directory independence, truthful trust posture, exact receipt fingerprinting, altered/missing/incompatible assets, unsafe paths, and zero network access.
negative: No provider may infer authenticated-release from local hashes, a self-authored manifest, or an unbound installation receipt.
No provider may use the current working directory, contact the network, execute bundled content, follow unsafe symlinks, or silently fall back after an explicitly selected source fails.
Legacy schema-v1 project packs cannot authorize a new Full run and must not be silently promoted to schema v2.
This Phase 2A.1 slice must not edit generic resources, detector, installer, qualification, project projection, current.json, frozen run binding, Full Start routing, or host adapters.
Missing, altered, incompatible, incomplete, unsafe, or conflicting bundle state must remain untouched and produce a typed fail-closed result.
